text.p: Bucharest first-tier Antibiotice pharmaceuticals company outperformed the bourse's other listings on Tuesday, helped by a special trade which raised its price and turnover.
Trading on the first tier was active, accounting for 91 percent of the session's turnover, which fell slightly to 7.9 billion lei from 8.5 billion previously.
But two unofficial indices were down, largely because the prices of the other three first-tier stocks fell in what traders said had been mainly speculative play.
The VAB and the BIG indices slipped by 1.8 percent each from the previous session. The BIG first-tier index fell by 2.26 percent to 3,285.23 points.

The Antibiotice special trade -- a large deal outside the market reported to the bourse later -- involved 47,590 shares traded at 5,800 lei each, which was also the stock's closing price. On Monday, Antibiotice closed at 5,750.
"Interest in the pharmaceuticals sector seems to be growing," a trader said.
Antibiotice turnover climbed to 3.3 billion lei from 1.7 billion on Monday.
Azomures fertiliser maker also had a special trade, with 107,198 shares worth a total of 385.9 million lei. It slipped 200 lei to 3,600.
Oltchim chemical plant ended 100 lei weaker at 2,350 and pharmaceuticals company Terapia, the fourth first-tier stock, lost 100 lei to close at 5,750.
A trader said the likelihood of further special trades made first-tier price forecasts difficult.
"The heavyweights will stay in the focus because the number of attractive smaller capitalisation stocks is low," he said.
Policolor was the only reasonably active listing on the second tier, with around 485 million lei in turnover and a close 50 lei stronger at 4,500.
Seven stocks had no trade and three companies were suspended pending announcements of 1996 economic results.
